card.title: Gauss law at work — line, sheet and capacitor

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Class 12 electrostatics upgrades Class 11: Coulomb's force becomes a FIELD mapped by E = F/q₀, Gauss law (flux = Q/ε₀) extracts the field of symmetric distributions without integration, potential V = W/q prices positions in energy per coulomb, and capacitors store that energy in the field itself. Line charges, charged sheets and parallel plates are the three Gauss showcases; dielectrics multiply capacitance by polarising against the applied field.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: F = kq₁q₂/r² · E = kQ/r² · Φ = Q/ε₀ · line: E = λ/2πε₀r · sheet: E = σ/2ε₀ · conductor surface: E = σ/ε₀ · V = kQ/r · C = ε₀A/d (×K with dielectric) · U = ½CV²

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Gauss is useful only with symmetry (spherical/cylindrical/planar) so E leaves the flux integral. V = kQ/r pins zero at infinity. C = ε₀A/d needs plate size ≫ separation (uniform field). Dielectric factor applies to fully-filled gaps; series/parallel rules assume ideal connections.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Inside a charged shell E = 0 while V stays constant — shielding. Infinite sheet gives distance-independent uniform E. Battery-connected vs isolated capacitor on dielectric insertion: V-fixed raises Q and U; Q-fixed drops V. Two equal charges midpoint: field cancels to zero.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Field of an infinite sheet, surface density σ: pillbox Gaussian surface straddling it — flux 2EA through both faces, enclosed σA → E = σ/2ε₀, uniform on each side, direction away for σ > 0. Same pillbox on a conductor (field inside zero) gives E = σ/ε₀ just outside.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Gauss yields total flux, not pointwise E, without symmetry. Point formulas fail inside continuous distributions. The dielectric constant is frequency- and field-dependent at extremes; breakdown caps every real capacitor. Electrostatics assumes static charges — moving charges add magnetism.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Point-charge flux: E·4πr² = (kQ/r²)·4πr² = Q/ε₀ — the r² cancels, so every enclosing surface passes identical flux. Superpose: Φ = ΣQ/ε₀. Capacitor: Gauss on one plate gives E = σ/ε₀, V = Ed, C = Q/V = ε₀A/d; charging incrementally, U = ∫(q/C)dq = Q²/2C.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Symmetry word → Gaussian surface matching it (sphere/pillbox/cylinder), flux = enclosed/ε₀, solve. 'Series or parallel?' → same Q (series) vs same V (parallel). Energy: pick ½CV², Q²/2C or ½QV by knowns.
